A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original density, runtime, diagonal-loading and step-size experiments for the proposed algorithms on real-world graphs.

after.justification: Section 4 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a stationarity finding concerning solutions obtained with different loading parameters.

M1.justification: The diagonally loaded relaxation, Frank-Wolfe algorithm with its two step-size options, and sigmoid constraint parameterization are unchanged. Explicit arbitrary tie breaking in v2 clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Densest k-Subgraph mining on Facebook, web-Stanford, com-Youtube, soc-Pokec, as-Skitter and com-Orkut. Table 1 and the experimental figures retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Greedy, rank-1 LRBO, L-ADMM and EXPP, together with the same density upper bound. Greedy remains omitted from the Facebook density panel but included in its runtime comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds a diagnostic assessing stationarity at λ=1 for solutions obtained with λ=10 or 100. The existing benchmark preprocessing, initialization, step-size settings, AdamW learning rate of 3 and 200-iteration budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a stationarity analysis connecting the high-loading solutions to the optimization landscape at λ=1. The existing loading-parameter and step-size sensitivity experiments are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for the experiments. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Section 4.4 newly reports that solutions obtained with λ=10 or 100 are not stationary at λ=1. All 16 experimental plot panels are identical across versions; v1 Figures 1–4 correspond to v2 Figures 2–5.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces a brief citation-based proof step with an explicit Lagrange-multiplier condition and algebraic derivation of f(x'')=f(x*) in v2 Equations 33–34. The theorem statements and substantive proofs in Appendices A, C and D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about the λ=1 tightness threshold, optimization landscape, two projection-free solvers and empirical scalability. The AAAI-version note does not correspond to new theorem statements relative to v1.

C2.justification: After Corollary 2, v2 clarifies that λ=1 is the general guarantee: the non-tightness argument for λ<1 concerns k<ω, while other sizes may admit tightness. Section 4.4 also interprets the new stationarity observation as evidence that increasing loading can introduce spurious local maxima.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code repository link on the first page and explicitly specifies arbitrary top-k tie breaking. The hardware, software, preprocessing, initialization and optimizer-setting disclosures otherwise match.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of convex DSG optimization with references [15–18], adds references to EXPP's journal parts, and positions the article relative to its AAAI preliminary version. The lecture-note reference supporting v1 Appendix B is removed. The main DkS positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct notation and wording, refine headings, and expand several explanations. Appendices move before acknowledgments and references. Most prose and the main scientific section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to an IEEE-style two-column layout, substantially reflowing text, equations, Algorithm 1, the table and figures. v2 adds a formulation-relationship diagram as Figure 1; existing experimental figures are resized, relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The code pointer, formulation diagram and clearer tightness qualification improve accessibility and precision. Expanded appendix reasoning and the stationarity observation add limited explanation and supporting evidence. These are modest gains because the algorithms, theorem statements and main numerical evidence were already present in v1.
